resolution: Both readers give the same fragment. The faded first letter of "pike" is p: reader A and the adjudicator read it certain, and the visible ink excludes g, q and y. The scan cannot separate œ from æ in the epithet. Under the editorial ruling that an ambiguous printed character takes the character the text means, the record has œ: both readers read it, Gutenberg prints "S. fœtens", and the epithet is foetens.
markupConvention: Genus names after "the genus" take gen, the corpus form (1,662 to 1); both readers wrote spn, which renders the same.
